nodes.summary: Let $f_1, \dots, f_s$ be functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and write $G(x, z)$ for the Grundy number of the chocolate bar with coordinates $x = (x_1, \dots, x_s) \in \mathbb{N}^s$ and width $z \in \mathbb{N}$. For all $x$ and $z$, $G(x, z)$ is the least natural number $m$ such that $m \ne G(x', z)$ for every $x'$ obtained from $x$ by replacing one coordinate $x_i$ with some $u < x_i$, and $m \ne G(x^{(w)}, w)$…
nodes.title: Mex recursion for the Grundy number of a chocolate bar

nodes.summary: For all functions $f_1, \dots, f_s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(f_1, \dots, f_s, 0, \dots, 0, 0)$, whose coordinates and width are all $0$, has Grundy number $0$: it is a single bitter square and has no move.
nodes.title: The single bitter square has Grundy number zero

nodes.summary: Let $f_1, \dots, f_s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. For coordinates $x = (x_1, \dots, x_s) \in \mathbb{N}^s$ and a width $z \in \mathbb{N}$, the position $(x, z)$ stands for the chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(f_1, \dots, f_s, x_1, \dots, x_s, z)$, whose column at width $w \le z$ extends $\min(f_t(w), x_t) + 1$ cells along axis $t$. A move either lowers one coordinate $x_i$ to some $u < x_i$, keeping the width $z$, or…
nodes.title: Grundy number of a chocolate bar

nodes.summary: Let $i$ be a natural number and let $z < z'$ be natural numbers. Then $\lfloor z / 2^i \rfloor = \lfloor z' / 2^i \rfloor$ if and only if there is a natural number $d$ with $d \cdot 2^i \le z$ and $z' < (d + 1) \cdot 2^i$.
nodes.title: Equal quotients by a power of two lie in one dyadic block

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $f_1, \dots, f_m : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property, and let $x_1, \dots, x_m, z, c$ be natural numbers with $x_t \le f_t(z)$ for all $t$ and $c < x_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus x_m \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ is nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or). Then either there are an index $i$ and some $u < x_i$ such that $c$ is the nim-sum $x_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus x_m \oplus z$ with $x_i$…
nodes.title: Mex step for chocolate bars with many functions

nodes.summary: Let $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property, and let $x, y, z, c$ be natural numbers with $x \le g(z)$, $y \le h(z)$ and $c < x \oplus y \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ is nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or). Then $c = u \oplus y \oplus z$ for some $u < x$, or $c = x \oplus v \oplus z$ for some $v < y$, or $c = \min(g(w), x) \oplus \min(h(w), y) \oplus w$ for some $w < z$.
nodes.title: Mex step for chocolate bars with two functions

nodes.summary: Let $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property, and let $x, z, c$ be natural numbers with $x \le g(z)$ and $c < x \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ is nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or). Then $c = u \oplus z$ for some $u < x$, or $c = \min(g(w), x) \oplus w$ for some $w < z$.
nodes.title: Mex step for chocolate bars with one function

nodes.summary: Let $z, z', i$ be natural numbers with $\lfloor z / 2^i \rfloor < \lfloor z' / 2^i \rfloor$. Then there are natural numbers $c$, $s$ and $t$ with $s \ge i$, $t < 2^s$, $z = c \cdot 2^{s+1} + t$ and $c \cdot 2^{s+1} + 2^s \le z'$.
nodes.title: Dyadic splitting of two numbers with different quotients

nodes.summary: Let $f_1, f_2, f_3, f_4 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone. Then all four have the NS property if and only if, for all natural numbers $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4, z$ with $x_t \le f_t(z)$ for every $t$, the Grundy number of the chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(f_1, f_2, f_3, f_4, x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4, z)$ equals $x_1 \oplus x_2 \oplus x_3 \oplus x_4 \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ is nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or).
nodes.title: Nim-sum Grundy numbers of chocolate bars with four functions

nodes.summary: Let $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone. Then $g$ and $h$ both have the NS property if and only if, for all natural numbers $x, y, z$ with $x \le g(z)$ and $y \le h(z)$, the Grundy number of the chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(g, h, x, y, z)$ equals $x \oplus y \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ is nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or).
nodes.title: Nim-sum Grundy numbers of chocolate bars with two functions

nodes.summary: For every natural number $c$, the constant function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with value $c$ has the NS property.
nodes.title: Constant functions have the NS property

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m \ge 1$, the function $x \mapsto \lfloor x / 2^m \rfloor$ on $\mathbb{N}$ has the NS property.
nodes.title: Halving functions have the NS property

nodes.summary: Let $z \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $h(a) \le h(b)$ whenever $a \le b \le z$, and $\lfloor h(a) / 2^{i-1} \rfloor = \lfloor h(b) / 2^{i-1} \rfloor$ whenever $a, b \le z$, $i \ge 1$ and $\lfloor a / 2^i \rfloor = \lfloor b / 2^i \rfloor$. Then the function sending $x$ to $h(x)$ for $x \le z$ and to $h(z)$ for $x > z$ has the NS property.
nodes.title: Constant extension preserves the NS property

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone. Then $f$ has the NS property if and only if, for all $x, z \in \mathbb{N}$ with $x \le f(z)$, the chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(f, 0, x, 0, z)$ of width $z$ (first function $f$, first coordinate $x$, second function constantly $0$, second coordinate $0$) has Grundy number $x \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ denotes nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or).
nodes.title: The NS property characterises nim-sum Grundy numbers of two-dimensional chocolate bars

nodes.summary: A function $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ has the *NS property* if it is monotone (weakly increasing) and, for all $z, z' \in \mathbb{N}$ and every natural number $i \ge 1$, $\lfloor z / 2^i \rfloor = \lfloor z' / 2^i \rfloor$ implies $\lfloor h(z) / 2^{i-1} \rfloor = \lfloor h(z') / 2^{i-1} \rfloor$.
nodes.title: NS property

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number with $k \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and let $F(w, x) = \lfloor (w + x) / k \rfloor$. For all $w, x, y \in \mathbb{N}$ with $y \le F(w, x)$, the three-dimensional chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(F, w, x, y)$ has Grundy number $0$ (is a P-position) if and only if $w \oplus x \oplus y = 0$, where $\oplus$ denotes nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or).
nodes.title: P-positions of a three-dimensional chocolate bar with floor-quotient height

nodes.summary: Let $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and $F : \mathbb{N}^s \to \mathbb{N}$, and write $G(x, y)$ for the Grundy number of the chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(F, x_1, \dots, x_s, y)$. For all $x \in \mathbb{N}^s$ and $y \in \mathbb{N}$, $G(x, y)$ is the least natural number $m$ such that $m \ne G(x', \min(F(x'), y))$ for every $x'$ obtained from $x$ by lowering one coordinate $x_i$ to some $u < x_i$, and $m \ne G(x, v)$ for every…
nodes.title: Mex recursion for chocolate bars with a height function

nodes.summary: For every $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $F : \mathbb{N}^s \to \mathbb{N}$, the chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(F, 0, \dots, 0, 0)$ has no move, so its Grundy number is $0$.
nodes.title: The single bitter cube has Grundy number zero

nodes.summary: Let $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and $F : \mathbb{N}^s \to \mathbb{N}$. The $(s + 1)$-dimensional chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(F, x_1, \dots, x_s, y)$ has, at each $u = (u_1, \dots, u_s)$ with $u_t \le x_t$ for all $t$, a column of height $\min(F(u), y) + 1$. nodes.title: Grundy number of a chocolate bar with a height function

nodes.title: Nim-sum sets under clamping by functions with the NS property

nodes.summary: Let $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property and let $x, z \in \mathbb{N}$ with $x \le g(z)$. Writing $\oplus$ for the nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or) of natural numbers, the sets $\{x \oplus w : w < z\}$ and $\{\min(g(w), x) \oplus w : w < z\}$ are equal, where $w$ ranges over the natural numbers.
nodes.title: Nim-sum image identity for one NS function

nodes.summary: Let $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property and let $x, y, z \in \mathbb{N}$ with $x \le g(z)$ and $y \le h(z)$. Writing $\oplus$ for the nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or) of natural numbers, the sets $\{x \oplus y \oplus w : w < z\}$ and $\{\min(g(w), x) \oplus \min(h(w), y) \oplus w : w < z\}$ are equal, where $w$ ranges over the natural numbers.
nodes.title: Nim-sum image identity for two NS functions

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone, with $f(x) \le 1$ for all $x$ and $f(x) = 1$ for some $x$. Then $f$ has the NS property if and only if there is an even $m \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $f$ is the indicator function of $\{n \in \mathbb{N} : n \ge m\}$, that is, $f(n) = 1$ for $n \ge m$ and $f(n) = 0$ for $n < m$.
nodes.title: Indicator functions with the NS property

nodes.summary: Let $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $F : \mathbb{N}^s \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone for the coordinatewise order, with $F(x) \le 1$ for all $x$. For $x \in \mathbb{N}^s$, $i < s$ and $t \in \mathbb{N}$ write $x[i \mapsto t]$ for $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate replaced by $t$, and suppose that for all $x$ and $i$ there is a $t$ with $F(x[i \mapsto t]) = 1$. nodes.title: Height-one chocolate bars with nim-sum Grundy numbers

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c, k \in \mathbb{N}$. If $\lfloor a / 2^k \rfloor = \lfloor b / 2^k \rfloor$, then $\lfloor \min(a, c) / 2^k \rfloor = \lfloor \min(b, c) / 2^k \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Taking a minimum preserves quotients by powers of two

nodes.summary: Let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property and let $z, z', k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \ge 1$ and $\lfloor z' / 2^k \rfloor = \lfloor z / 2^k \rfloor$. Then for every $y \in \mathbb{N}$, $\lfloor \min(h(z'), y) / 2^{k-1} \rfloor = \lfloor \min(h(z), y) / 2^{k-1} \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Quotients of a truncated NS function by powers of two

nodes.title: Nim with a restricted pass

nodes.summary: For every $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $m, x \in \mathbb{N}^s$, the pass indicator of $m$ at $x$ is at most $1$; that is, it takes values in $\{0, 1\}$.
nodes.title: The Nim pass indicator is at most one

nodes.summary: Let $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}^s$ with $m_i > 0$ for every $i < s$, and let $F : \mathbb{N}^s \to \mathbb{N}$ be the pass indicator of $m$: $F(x) = 1$ if $m_j \le x_j$ for some $j$, and $F(x) = 0$ otherwise. For $x \in \mathbb{N}^s$, $i < s$ and $t \in \mathbb{N}$ write $x[i \mapsto t]$ for $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate replaced by $t$. Then the following are equivalent: (a) for all…
nodes.title: Sections of the Nim pass indicator with the NS property

nodes.summary: Let $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}^s$ with $m_i > 0$ for every $i < s$. Then the pass indicator of $m$ takes the value $0$ at the zero tuple $(0, \dots, 0)$.
nodes.title: The pass is unavailable from the empty position

nodes.summary: For $s$ piles with thresholds $m_0, \dots, m_{s-1}$ and pile sizes $x_0, \dots, x_{s-1}$ (natural numbers), the pass indicator is $1$ if $m_j \le x_j$ for some pile $j$ (the pass may be used), and $0$ if $x_j < m_j$ for every pile $j$.
nodes.title: Pass indicator of Nim with a restricted pass

nodes.summary: The identity function on the natural numbers does not have the NS property: $\lfloor 0/2 \rfloor = \lfloor 1/2 \rfloor$, but $0 \ne 1$.
nodes.title: The identity function lacks the NS property

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
